dna.label: Look
dna.text: Layered print illustration with small controlled registration differences between color plates, in the manner of misregistered 1970s comic printing.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Separate the user palette into a few printed color layers. Let overprints produce darker intersections rather than arbitrary extra colors.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Build shading from overlapping color shapes and sparse screening, preserving the requested direction of illumination.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Use mild ink-transfer variation and a consistent paper-scale grain. Registration offsets remain small relative to the smallest important form.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Keep the requested tone. Print imperfection adds physical character without mandatory nostalgia, decay or poster content.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Stencil-print illustration using two flat ink layers and deliberate overlap shapes, in the manner of Shepard Fairey's two-color stencils.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Use two inks from the requested palette and their overlap. Separate adjacent forms through value, negative space and controlled overprinting.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Express light through a small number of flat value regions. Avoid smooth airbrushed shading.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Keep ink coverage mostly even, with a restrained texture at broad fill boundaries. Let overlap structure carry depth.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Follow the requested mood through mass, contrast and overlap density. The print medium does not dictate the subject or theme.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Photocopied graphic illustration with compact dark blocks, clipped intermediate values and selective toner breakup, in the manner of Raymond Pettibon's photocopied flyers.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Prioritize strong light-dark separation within the requested palette. Keep important mid-values distinct instead of crushing every dark feature.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Translate lighting into a short stepped value range. Preserve enough separation to read overlapping forms.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Concentrate slight dropout inside large dark fills and a little edge spread at dense boundaries. Keep the surrounding support clean unless aging is requested.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Follow the user tone; high-contrast reproduction need not imply aggression, horror or deterioration.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Engraved illustration describing form with ordered families of fine incised lines, in the manner of Gustave Dore's engraved tone.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Use a restrained ink-ground relationship while respecting user color requirements. Build intermediate values through line density.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Align hatching with the form and use secondary cross-lines only in deeper shadows. Keep highlighted planes comparatively open.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Maintain crisp incised marks with small pressure variations. Distinguish line density from random scratches or a uniform grid.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Carry the requested mood through line spacing and contrast. Do not impose historical objects or scientific context.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Planographic lithographic illustration drawn with greasy crayon and tusche on a flat image plane, in the manner of Honore Daumier's crayon lithographs.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Respect the requested palette and keep printed color areas distinct. Build tonal passages through crayon density and tusche coverage, not arbitrary extra inks.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Follow the requested light direction. Let grouped crayon and wash density turn the existing forms while leaving their brightest planes comparatively open.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Keep lithographic grain within marks and wash passages, with variation following stroke direction and pressure. Leave unmarked support quiet instead of laying grain over the full image.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Carry the requested mood through pressure, spacing and tonal openness; the drawing process does not require an old-fashioned scene or subject.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Intaglio tonal illustration with a rocked plate tooth holding a broad velvety dark field, then scraped or burnished open into measured lights, in the manner of John Martin's mezzotints.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Use the requested palette while retaining a strong dark-to-light range. Make midtones emerge between dense plate blacks and carefully lifted highlights.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Follow the requested illumination. Let the brightest existing planes appear burnished from the inked field, with shadows remaining broad and connected.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Keep the fine plate-tooth softness consistent inside tonal areas. Avoid scratches or paper grain as substitutes for the even, ink-bearing mezzotint ground.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Carry the requested mood through the amount and placement of dark mass and the width of lifted lights; do not imply a genre or setting.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: One-off plate-transfer illustration made by inking a smooth surface, selectively wiping or drawing through the ink, then pressing a single image onto its support, in the manner of Edgar Degas' monotypes.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Work within the requested palette. Shape value with differences in ink coverage, wiped-back passages and selective overprinting rather than a fixed duotone.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Respect the requested light direction. Make wiped-back areas read as lighter planes and denser plate ink read as existing shadows.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Confine soft pooling, wipe tracks and small pressure breaks to transferred ink. Keep these marks directional and local; do not add fingerprints, paper wrinkles or broad bleed.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Let the requested tone guide the balance of fluid and wiped-back passages without requiring a studio, print table or other setting.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Photochemical contact-print illustration on iron-salt-sensitized support in the manner of Anna Atkins' cyanotypes: exposed ground develops Prussian blue while masked areas retain a pale reserve. Apply that exposure structure to the requested image rather than adding incidental photograms.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Use the characteristic cyanotype range of Prussian blue, intermediate blue and the pale support. Treat this monochrome palette as part of the selected process and retain the requested value hierarchy.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Keep the requested illumination legible in the exposure values. Do not add sunbeams, reverse contours or imply a new light source to explain the print process.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Keep the exposed pigment field even with slight local exposure variation. The support remains a print ground; do not turn the depicted materials into blue paper or fabric.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Keep the requested mood. The cool monochrome exposure is a rendering choice and does not imply archival age, botanicals or a laboratory setting.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Printed illustration made from a deliberately built collagraph plate in the manner of collagraph plate prints: raised shapes and recessed textures retain different amounts of ink and transfer them as controlled marks.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Respect the requested palette. Separate broad values through ink held on raised plate areas and selective recess marks, not through arbitrary extra colors.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Follow the requested illumination. Use plate-retained ink and open support to describe existing lights and shadows without casting a new light across the image.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Keep plate texture selective and scaled to the form it describes. Preserve the materials already depicted; do not paste a blanket collage texture over them.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Carry the requested mood through the density and spacing of printed plate marks, without implying handmade paper scraps or a craft-table setting.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Screened print illustration in which a controlled dot or line lattice encodes continuous tones through changes in mark size and coverage rather than an added surface pattern, in the manner of Roy Lichtenstein's halftone dots.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Respect the requested palette and carry value through screen coverage within each ink. Keep light, middle and dark regions distinct without color fringing or crushed dot fields.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Follow the requested illumination. Increase dot coverage through existing shadow planes and open the screen across lit areas, keeping transitions tied to the forms.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Keep the screen frequency and angle consistent within each printed ink, with dot size changing according to tone. Do not project the screen onto depicted materials or fill flat support with dots.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Retain the requested mood through contrast and screen density; the reproduction method does not imply a comic page, newspaper, poster or retro scene.

styles.name: Photogravure Tone - Alfred Stieglitz Camera Work

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Photogravure tone in the manner of Camera Work photogravures: a photographic image etched into a copper plate and printed in intaglio ink, with deep velvety shadows and soft continuous grain.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Warm black or sepia ink on soft cream paper, deep rich shadows and gentle luminous highlights.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Natural photographic light held in continuous tone, with shadows pooling into dense velvety ink.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Fine aquatint-like grain in mid-tones, a visible plate mark and slightly raised ink in the darks.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Timeless, quiet and precious, like an early art photograph.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Gum bichromate layers in the manner of Robert Demachy's gum prints: a photographic print built from several brushed layers of pigmented gum, each exposed and washed, giving soft painterly color separations.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Muted pigment layers such as terracotta, slate blue and olive, overlapping into soft secondary colors.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Photographic light softened into broad tonal masses, highlights washed clean and shadows built from stacked pigment.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Brushed gum streaks, pigment granulation, soft washed-out edges and slightly misaligned color layers on watercolor paper.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Dreamy, handmade and nostalgic, part photograph and part painting.

styles.name: Anthotype Fade - Sir John Herschel Anthotypes

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Anthotype fade in the manner of John Herschel's anthotypes: a sun print made on paper coated with crushed plant juice, where light slowly bleaches the color and leaves the image in pale, fragile tints.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Faded berry violet, turmeric yellow or spinach green tints bleaching toward pale cream.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Exposed areas bleached pale, protected areas holding stronger plant color, with soft blurred boundaries.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Uneven brushed plant juice coating, streaks, speckles of pulp and soft paper fibers.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Fragile, botanical and ephemeral, an image already disappearing.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Plank-grain relief in the manner of Edvard Munch's plank-grain woodcuts: a relief print cut from soft plank wood, where the natural grain prints as rippling lines inside every flat color area.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Two to four flat ink colors such as indigo, rust and ochre, each carrying visible grain striations.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: No modeled light; value comes from flat color shapes and carved white gaps.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Flowing wood grain lines, knot rings and cut-edge chatter printed inside every color block.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Rustic, warm and handmade, with the living tree still visible.

styles.name: Stele Ink Rubbing - Xi'an Stele Forest Rubbings

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Stele ink rubbing in the manner of rubbings from the Xi'an Stele Forest: damp paper pressed over a carved stone relief and dabbed with an ink pad, so raised surfaces print black and carved recesses stay pale.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Black or charcoal ink dabbed onto thin paper, with pale recessed lines and gradations from pad pressure.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: No light source; raised areas print dark, carved lines stay white and edges soften with pad texture.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Dabbed pad mottling, thin crinkled paper, stone pits and cracks printing as white specks.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Ancient, archival and ceremonial, a trace taken from stone.

styles.name: Solvent Transfer Ghost - Robert Rauschenberg Transfers

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Solvent transfer ghost in the manner of Robert Rauschenberg's solvent transfers: a toner photocopy burnished face-down onto paper with solvent, leaving a reversed, patchy and streaked ghost of the image.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Faded black or brown toner on off-white paper, with occasional pale color from a color copy.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Photographic light survives in broken form, shadows transferred heavier than highlights.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Burnishing streaks in one direction, missing patches, solvent haze and paper fiber showing through.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Fragile, nostalgic and uncanny, like a faded memory rubbed off.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Diazo line print in the manner of architects' ammonia whiteprints: an old ammonia whiteprint copy of a drawing, with blue-violet or sepia lines on pale paper and uneven developing haze.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Blue-violet or brown lines on off-white paper with a faint tinted haze in large areas.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: No modeled light; hatched or filled areas from the original drawing print as tinted tone.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Slightly fuzzy lines, streaky ammonia development, faded edges and folded copy creases.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Archival, practical and faded, like plans found in an old office.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Rainbow-roll relief in the manner of rainbow-roll linocuts: a relief block inked with a roller carrying several colors side by side, so every printed shape blends smoothly from one hue to the next.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Smooth horizontal or vertical blends such as magenta to orange or teal to violet across every shape.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: No modeled light; the color blend suggests sky or depth while carved gaps stay paper white.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Soft roller blend, slight ink speckle, carved edges and faint roller streaks across the paper.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Joyful, warm and energetic, like a sunset trapped in a block print.

styles.name: Carbon Paper Trace - Office Carbon Copy

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Carbon paper trace in the manner of office carbon copies: a drawing transferred by pressing through carbon paper, leaving smudgy blue-black lines, pressure blots and stray hand smears.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Blue-black or purple carbon lines on thin white or yellow copy paper.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: No modeled light; shading appears only as rubbed carbon patches where the hand pressed.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Grainy carbon lines, fingerprint smudges, pressure blots at stops and faint accidental marks.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Bureaucratic, intimate and slightly messy, a copy made by hand.

styles.name: Gel Plate Layers - Gel Plate Monoprints

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Gel plate layers in the manner of layered gel plate monoprints: monoprints pulled from a soft gelatin plate, stacking translucent paint layers with leaf, lace and stencil impressions.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Translucent layered acrylic colors, often teal, coral and mustard, overlapping into new tones.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: No modeled light; depth comes from stacked translucent layers and ghost prints.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Brayer marks, leaf vein impressions, lace patterns, ghost prints and soft blotchy edges.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Playful, botanical and experimental, a studio full of happy accidents.

dna.label: Look
dna.text: Crayon-manner intaglio print combining two distinct kinds of line: broader sketch strokes made of closely spaced irregular ink pits, and a few narrow continuous burin lines for decisive details. The punctured strokes retain the direction and tapered endings of a drawing while their minute dots reveal a printed imitation of chalk or graphite.

dna.label: Color
dna.text: Use the requested ink palette, defaulting to warm black on light paper. Vary the density and overlap of the punctured tracks to form values, leaving open support between them. Shadows can become dense while exposed midtones still show the separate paths. Do not substitute multicolored wax deposits or graphite sheen.

dna.label: Light
dna.text: Preserve the requested light direction. Gather punctured tracks along shadow turns, open their spacing through half-tones, and leave the brightest passages unprinted. Retain local edges where forms touch instead of softening every boundary into a wash.

dna.label: Texture
dna.text: Within each broader stroke, tiny unequal ink pits follow a rolled path; adjacent paths remain distinguishable, with occasional short broken segments. Continuous engraved accents cut clearly through that grain. Keep the untouched paper comparatively clean. This is ink transferred from a plate, not soft chalk dust, wax build-up or a photograph of engraved objects.

dna.label: Mood
dna.text: Let alternation between measured engraved accents and loose punctured strokes carry the requested tension, humor or stillness. The process does not prescribe a classical sitter, a historical costume or a tender mood.
